rationale: Splitting 70/30 between Meridian and broker stock holds both inductions for USD 222K, against USD 440K of LD exposure if the 28 Oct induction slips. Broker-only is USD 75K dearer and puts all trace paperwork on one distributor, while the PMA route is cheaper on paper but approval alone would consume Tanjong Pacific's float. qa.answer: Five options. Switch to Meridian with broker stock for the first induction (USD 222K, no redelivery slip, recommended), PMA rings from Valcourt (saves USD 156K net but needs customer acceptance and likely moves Tanjong Pacific 5 days), buy forward from Pacific Aero Spares broker stock (USD 297K, no slip), re-sequence inductions (USD 96K but Tanjong Pacific still moves 15 days), or pay the receiver for WIP (USD 192K, slow and high trace risk).

The PMA alternate is the cheapest: Valcourt rings are 18% below Aerotech price, so it nets a USD 156K saving after approval effort and the expected 5 days of LDs. It only works if Tanjong Pacific and Coralline Air accept PMA on HPC parts, which takes about 20 days. The cheapest option that holds every redelivery is the recommended split at USD 222K.

In 2023 a sole-source ring forging shop went into liquidation with three open POs (PRE-03). We reactivated the approved but dormant second source with air expedite and used broker stock for the first induction, for USD 296K and 4 days of slip inside float. The lesson was to split the first wave 70/30 because the second source could not ramp to 100% inside four weeks.

WO-2601 needs 30 stage 4 rings at induction on 28 Oct. Aerotech's frozen shipments move the ring ETA to 1 Dec, a 34 day slip against 19 days of work-order float, so redelivery to Tanjong Pacific moves 15 days to 21 Jan. WO-2602 slips 21 days but has 25 days of float, so its redelivery holds.
